before_reproduction.finding: The old GLBs contained 192 exact duplicate triangle groups in symmetric fan-bar construction, coplanar/near-coplanar face and relief surfaces, and a non-watertight core. These model-side defects were present in both viewers and were sufficient to create angle-dependent shimmer or apparent transparency.

root_causes: Eight full 180-degree-symmetric fan bars produced duplicate coincident triangles.
The prior Three.js-style box core was not watertight after export.
Perimeter seams, cover seams, rear handle mounts, hubs, fasteners, and source cards used overlapping or unstable depth layers.
repairs: Replaced the chassis core with a custom indexed 8-vertex/12-triangle watertight outward shell.
Reduced eight redundant full fan bars to four bars while retaining eight visible spokes, eliminating all 192 duplicate groups.
Removed perimeter and side-cover geometry already represented by the source-locked textures.
Moved fan hubs, rear handle mounts, side/top fasteners, and card/backing relationships to stable, non-competing depth levels.
Preserved the source-locked PNGs and regenerated standard/web from identical visible geometry.

standard_and_web.materials: OPAQUE only; baseColor alpha 1; doubleSided false

authenticity_conclusion: PASS_WITH_BOTTOM_FALLBACK for the frozen delivery subject: all front, user-locked rear, left/right, and top identity-bearing features match their locked sources. No non-bottom gap remains relative to that subject.
warnings_and_residual_risk: The underside is a conservative opaque fallback with no unsupported detail.

The user-locked rear conflicts with Fortinet's catalog factory rear. The delivered asset intentionally follows the user's row-3 delivery appearance and does not claim that rear as catalog-authoritative.
Twenty-four reported coplanar contacts are sub-1 mm^2 solid fan/handle/bar joints; hazardous visible draw-order pairs are zero.
